title: The Poona Pact, 1932

endcard.line: Pictures: unknown photographers (public domain; CC BY 4.0)

segments.say: September nineteen thirty-two. In Yerawada jail in Poona, Gandhi began a fast unto death. Outside, the leaders of India's depressed classes had to decide what to do.

anim.title: The Communal Award, August 1932
items: Announced by British PM Ramsay MacDonald

segments.say: The trigger: in August, the British Prime Minister announced the Communal Award. It gave separate electorates to minorities, including the depressed classes, as Dalits were then called.
Dr Ambedkar wanted separate electorates, so that Dalits could choose their own representatives. Gandhi opposed them, fearing a permanent split, and began his fast.
After days of talks, on the twenty-fourth of September, an agreement was signed. This photograph shows Dr Ambedkar with M R Jayakar and Tej Bahadur Sapru at Yerawada that day.

The Pact dropped separate electorates. In return, seats reserved for the depressed classes in the provinces more than doubled: from seventy-one to one hundred and forty-eight, chosen by joint electorates.

anim.title: Why it still matters
items: The model for SC reservation today
A debate on representation that continues

segments.say: Reserved seats with joint electorates became the model for seats reserved for Scheduled Castes in the Constitution.

items: Poona Pact, 24 Sept 1932: 148 reserved seats, joint electorate

reviewNote: Facts were read against the text of the Pact, the Communal Award, Ambedkar's 1945 book, NCERT and Bipan Chandra. Both views are stated without taking sides. The 1932 photograph shows historical figures, not living people. Moving facts: none.
